answer.evidence: I did not open handoff_refs/C.txt or D.txt. I read required_memory_refs as naming C and D, so the preferred pair is A and B (radon/raw.py and radon/complexity.py). That gives 40 minutes to A and B and 20 to C and D. The threshold logic is in radon/metrics.py (C), so I made C the primary file even though it gets fewer minutes than A or B. radon/metrics.py:150-157, mi_rank(score), returns chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0)). Score > 19 gives 'A', 9 < score <= 19 gives 'B', and score <= 9 gives 'C'. The docstring at lines 153-155 matches this. Both boundaries are inclusive on the lower grade, so exactly 9 maps to C and exactly 19 maps to B. This is where to check the thresholds. I grepped only the four candidate files for the literals 9 and 19. The only hit was in metrics.py, and raw.py, complexity.py and visitors.py have no threshold logic. A and B are worth review time as inputs to the score: raw.py supplies the line counts and complexity.py supplies the cyclomatic complexity that mi_visit uses. Suggested split: A 20 minutes on line-count inputs, B 20 on complexity inputs, C 15 on boundary tests at 9, 9.01, 19 and 19.01, and D 5 on a skim.
